prompt.zh: 我希望自己一直往上走，变得更强一点。
prompt.en: I want to keep moving forward and become a little stronger.

prompt.zh: 我心里一直有想认真追求的东西。

paragraphs.zh: 认真的吗？我真的是傻逼吗？
paragraphs.en: Seriously? Am I really that much of an idiot?

paragraphs.zh: 维度命中度较高，当前结果可视为你的第一人格画像。
paragraphs.en: A relatively close match across the model's dimensions; this is the first profile selected for this attempt.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了百万年一遇的【IMSB】人格。IMSB 不是简单的“自卑”，而是一种把自己当项目经理、审计员、甲方和黑粉同时使用的顶级内耗体质。别人做错事会安慰自己“没事，下次再来”，您做错一点点，脑内已经自动召开事故复盘会：事故经过、责任划分、整改方案、永久警示，全都给自己安排得明明白白。您最大的特长，就是在事情还没开始之前，先把自己骂到像已经失败了三次。但神奇的是，您并不是真的躺平。恰恰相反，您对“变强”这件事极其认真，只是方式过于残暴。别人靠鼓励，您靠自我拷打；别人靠外部监督，您靠灵魂皮鞭。面对喜欢的人，您心里能同时住着两个极端角色：一个喊“冲啊，去要微信，去吃饭，去大声说出来”，另一个冷笑着说“人家凭什么看得上你，你过去就是自取其辱”。结果通常是：站在原地，看着机会路过，再默默打开搜索框输入“如何克服社交恐惧和过度自我怀疑”。您不是废，您只是把自己要求得像军工验收。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: the original joke presents IMSB as a personality encountered once in a million years. IMSB is more than ordinary self-doubt. It is the exhausting arrangement of treating yourself as project manager, auditor, demanding client and hostile critic all at once. When someone else makes a mistake, you can say, ‘Never mind; try again next time.’ When you make even a small error, an incident review opens in your head: what happened, who was responsible, the corrective plan and the permanent warning are all ready. Your special trick is to criticise yourself before anything has started, as though you had already failed three times. Yet you are not simply giving up. Becoming stronger matters to you; your way of pursuing it is just unusually harsh. Other people use encouragement or outside supervision. You use an internal interrogation and a metaphorical whip. Around someone you like, two voices can appear together. One says, ‘Go on: ask to stay in touch, suggest a meal, say what you feel.’ The other says, ‘Why would they like you? You would only embarrass yourself.’ You may stay where you are, watch the opportunity pass and quietly search for help with social anxiety and excessive self-doubt. The closing joke is that you are not useless: you are holding yourself to the standard of a military equipment inspection. These are the original profile's exaggerated scenes and metaphors, not findings about rarity, a diagnosis or a measurement of your worth.

title.en: All fifteen descriptions in the original portrait

paragraphs.zh: 自尊自信：你对自己的评价标准偏高，容易把小波动也读成大问题。
paragraphs.en: Self-evaluation: You set a high standard for yourself and can read a small fluctuation as a much larger problem.

paragraphs.zh: 自我清晰度：你大致知道自己是什么路数，只是偶尔会在情绪上打个晃。
paragraphs.en: Sense of self: You broadly know your own way of doing things, even if your feelings sometimes wobble.

paragraphs.zh: 核心价值：你心里通常有一套自己的排序，做事不会完全靠别人推着走。
paragraphs.en: Core values: You usually have priorities of your own and do not rely entirely on other people to move you along.

paragraphs.zh: 依恋安全感：你在关系里的安全感有波动，但整体还算能把自己拉回来。
paragraphs.en: Relationship security: Your sense of security in relationships fluctuates, but you can generally bring yourself back.

paragraphs.zh: 情感投入度：你愿意投入情绪，但也会给自己留一点回旋空间。
paragraphs.en: Emotional investment: You are willing to invest emotionally while keeping a little room to adjust.

paragraphs.zh: 边界与依赖：你对边界和依赖的拿捏，不会一路失控，也不会完全无感。
paragraphs.en: Boundaries and dependence: Your approach to boundaries and dependence is neither continually out of control nor entirely detached.

paragraphs.zh: 世界观倾向：你看世界时既会带入感受，也会保留一点自己的判断。
paragraphs.en: View of the world: You bring feelings into your view of the world while retaining some judgement of your own.

paragraphs.zh: 规则与灵活度：你对规则不是死守，也不是彻底摆烂，更多是按场景调节。
paragraphs.en: Rules and flexibility: You neither follow rules rigidly nor abandon them entirely; you tend to adjust to the situation.

paragraphs.zh: 人生意义感：你会认真想人生和意义，只是有时想太多也会把自己绕进去。
paragraphs.en: Life and meaning: You think seriously about life and meaning, although too much thinking can sometimes tie you in knots.

paragraphs.zh: 动机导向：你有自己的动机来源，只是发力方式不总是同一种。
paragraphs.en: Sources of motivation: You have sources of motivation of your own, but they do not always express themselves in the same way.

paragraphs.zh: 决策风格：你做决定时会混合理性、直觉和当下状态，不算单线程。
paragraphs.en: Decision style: Your decisions mix reasoning, intuition and your present state rather than following a single track.

paragraphs.zh: 执行模式：你推进事情的方式有弹性，能冲也能缓，不是一种节奏打天下。
paragraphs.en: Way of acting: Your way of moving things forward is flexible: sometimes you push and sometimes you slow down.

paragraphs.zh: 社交主动性：你社交时不一定最响，但会按照自己舒服的方式进入场子。
paragraphs.en: Social initiative: You need not be the loudest person in a group; you join in in a way that feels comfortable to you.

paragraphs.zh: 人际边界感：你的人际边界感基本在线，知道什么时候靠近、什么时候退开。
paragraphs.en: Interpersonal boundaries: You generally have a sense of interpersonal boundaries and know when to approach or step back.

paragraphs.zh: 表达与真实度：你表达真实感时会留白，很多想法更习惯先在心里过一遍。
paragraphs.en: Authentic expression: You leave some things unsaid when expressing yourself and prefer to consider many thoughts privately first.

title.zh: 补充情境：把画像放回日常
title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: Imagine sending a draft and later noticing one unclear sentence. There is a concrete job available: clarify the sentence or ask whether it caused confusion. Self-critical review can add a second job that was never requested, such as rehearsing what the sentence supposedly proves about your overall competence or how the reader must now see you.
paragraphs.zh: 比如发出一份初稿后，发现一句话不够清楚。眼前有个具体任务：补清那句话，或确认它是否造成误解。苛刻复盘却可能额外加上一项没人要求的工作：反复想这句话证明自己整体有多差，或收件人现在一定怎样看自己。

paragraphs.en: Those are different questions. A reader asking for a clearer example has not necessarily made a judgment about you as a person. Equally, a real error does not disappear because the quiz calls your response a theme. Look at the actual comment, consequence and correction needed before treating the whole situation as a personal verdict.
paragraphs.zh: 这是两种不同的问题。读者希望例子更清楚，不一定是在评价你这个人；另一方面，游戏把反应叫作一个主题，也不会让真实错误消失。先看实际反馈、后果和需要补的动作，再决定是否有必要给整件事下一个关于自己的总判决。

paragraphs.en: Careful review has a practical use when it identifies something specific that can be checked. You might notice a missing assumption, an ambiguous promise or a step that needs another pair of eyes. The nickname does not prove this skill, but a particular example may show you where reviewing was useful.
paragraphs.zh: 复盘能指出一件可核对的具体事情时，就有实际用途：比如漏掉一个条件、承诺不够明确，或某一步需要再请人看一眼。昵称不能证明你具有这种能力，但具体例子可以帮助你看出哪一次检查确实有用。

paragraphs.en: The cost can appear when the standard keeps moving after the relevant check is complete. Another reread may offer no new information while delaying the next task. Distinguish a correction that changes the work from a repeated accusation that only changes the mood in which you are doing it. The result cannot make that distinction for you.
paragraphs.zh: 代价可能出现在检查已经做完、标准却仍不断后退的时候。又读一遍未必带来新信息，却会推迟下一件事。可以区分真正改变作品的修改，和只改变做事心情的重复责备；这份结果不能代你完成这个区分。

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary, low-stakes task, write down the issue, one check and a stopping condition. An example is: “The instruction may be unclear; ask one reader to describe the next step; revise if that step differs from what I intended.” The point is to inspect an actual task, not to use a quiz result as a reason to become a different person.
paragraphs.zh: 可以选一件普通、低风险的小事，记下问题、一次核对和停止条件。比如：“说明可能不清楚；请一位读者说出下一步；如果与我的本意不同，再改。”目的是看清一项实际任务，而不是因为游戏结果就要求自己变成另一种人。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, notice whether another round would supply new information. If circumstances change, a new review may be appropriate. If nothing changes except the wording of the accusation, you can leave that accusation out of the task list. This is an optional reflection, not a treatment or a promise that one exercise will change distress.
paragraphs.zh: 事后可以看看：再来一轮能否获得新信息？情况变了，重新检查可能合理；如果变化的只是责备自己的说法，可以不把那句责备继续列进任务清单。这只是可选的日常观察，不是治疗，也不保证一次练习会改变困扰。
31题选项沿原模型贡献固定影响值，分别取均值并转换为15维读数；画像由原固定规则选出。同一组完整答案的结果固定，不会在提交时随机抽取。
paragraphs.en: The original options contribute fixed impact values. The model averages them and maps them to fifteen readouts, then selects a profile through its original deterministic rule. The same complete answers give the same result, rather than drawing a new result at submission.

paragraphs.zh: 匹配展示值及预设稀有度沿用原玩法，前者不是准确率，后者不是人口统计。原文中的“最稀有”等是趣味夸张；15维分段是模型显示，不作人群高低或诊断阈值。
paragraphs.en: The match display and preset rarity belong to the original game. The match is not an accuracy rate; preset rarity is not a population statistic. Expressions such as “rarest” in the original story are comic exaggerations. Fifteen-dimension display bands are model displays, not population ranks or diagnostic cutoffs.

paragraphs.zh: 本页是所有人都能阅读的公开说明，不包含你的答卷、分数或私人结果。完整画像和15维读法无需注册或继续其他测评即可阅读。
paragraphs.en: This public guide is identical for everyone and contains no personal answers, scores or private result. The complete portrait and all fifteen descriptions are readable without signup or taking another assessment.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【BOSS】人格。BOSS 型人格手里仿佛永远拿着一个无形方向盘：哪怕油箱见红，导航乱报，路况稀烂，您也会很平静地吐出三个字，“我来开”。别人看到混乱会头大，您看到混乱会起精神；别人问“怎么办”，您已经在脑内排完优先级、资源表和风险列表。您不是喜欢命令人，您只是对“事情烂在眼前”这件事过敏。BOSS 看世界，很像满级玩家在看新手教程。效率是您的宗教，秩序是您的呼吸，自我突破则是您的日常小零食。普通人学一门新技能，您会顺手再报两个证、开三个表、做一份路线图，还觉得这只是“正常推进”。您身上的压迫感并不一定来自脾气，而是来自一种天然的“向上定律”：您一出场，空气都会自动进入 KPI 模式。您不是在卷，您只是觉得“能做更好为什么不做”。别人说您狠，您会淡淡看他一眼：不是我太猛，是你太松。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew the BOSS profile. This character seems to hold an invisible steering wheel at all times. The fuel light can be on, the navigation can be confused and the road can be terrible, yet the response is still a calm ‘I will drive.’ Where other people see chaos and get a headache, BOSS becomes alert. Before someone finishes asking what to do, priorities, resources and risks are already being arranged in the character's head. The joke is not a love of giving orders so much as an allergy to watching a situation fall apart. BOSS looks at the world as a highly experienced player might look at a beginner's tutorial: efficiency becomes a religion, order a way of breathing, and improving oneself a daily snack. Someone else learns a new skill; BOSS also signs up for two qualifications, starts three spreadsheets and drafts a route map, then calls it normal progress. The pressure this character creates does not always come from a temper. It comes from an exaggerated upward pull: once BOSS enters the room, even the air seems to acquire performance targets. In this story, doing something better is reason enough to try. When someone calls the character too intense, the imagined answer is, ‘Perhaps I am not too fierce; perhaps you are too relaxed.’ Read the confident tone as part of the original entertainment portrait. Receiving BOSS does not prove leadership skill, workplace performance or superiority over anyone else.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: Imagine several friends arranging a shared event. Everyone has preferences, but nobody has written down a first proposal. You suggest a time, a modest budget and two tasks that need owners, then ask what needs changing. Here, taking initiative means making a proposal available for discussion rather than treating silence as permission to decide for everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 比如几位朋友商量一次共同活动，人人有偏好，却没人整理第一版方案。你提出时间、小范围预算，以及两项需要分工的事情，再问哪些地方要改。这里的主动，是拿出可讨论的草案，而不是把别人没说话当作替所有人拍板的许可。

paragraphs.en: A different situation may already have a responsible organizer. Adding a second plan without checking can duplicate work or create confusion. The same urge to move things forward can then be expressed by asking what help is actually useful. A theme label does not settle who has authority in a real group.
paragraphs.zh: 另一种情况是现场已有负责组织的人。没核对就再加一套安排，可能重复劳动或造成混乱。相同的推进愿望，此时也可以表现为先问到底需要哪种帮助。一个主题标签不能决定现实群体里谁有决定权。

paragraphs.en: A visible next step can help people discover where they agree and what information is missing. A short proposal is especially different from a demand when others can reject or revise it. Look for evidence that the shared task became clearer; do not assume initiative itself is always a contribution.
paragraphs.zh: 一个可见的下一步，有时能让大家发现哪些地方一致、还缺什么信息。允许别人否决或修改时，简短提案才更像提案，而不是命令。可以看共同任务是否真的更清楚，而不要预设只要主动就一定是在贡献。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when speed leaves too little room for another person’s constraint. A deadline you suggest may not be feasible, and a role you find obvious may require consent or expertise. If disagreement appears, it is information about the arrangement, not proof that others are unmotivated or that you must push harder.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在速度挤掉了他人限制的时候。你提的期限未必可行，你觉得明显的分工也可能需要对方同意或具备相应知识。出现不同意见，是关于安排的新信息，不是别人不积极、或你必须更用力推的证据。

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes shared task, try a proposal with three parts: the next action, what you are volunteering to do and what still needs agreement. For example: “I can draft the list tonight. Would this date work, and is anything important missing?” That keeps the offer observable without claiming a general leadership trait.
paragraphs.zh: 在一件低风险共同任务里，可以试着把提案拆成三部分：下一步是什么、自己愿意做什么、什么仍需商量。比如：“今晚我可以先列清单。这个日期适合吗，有没有漏掉的重要事？”这样能观察一项具体提议，不必先给自己认领领导特质。

paragraphs.en: Check whether others could disagree or change the proposal without needing to defend themselves. If not, reduce the size of the decision or ask one genuine question before continuing. Success here means learning what the group needs, not persuading everyone or proving that an Leader result was accurate.
paragraphs.zh: 之后可以核对：别人是否能不同意或修改，而不必先为自己辩护？如果不能，可以缩小决定范围，或先真诚地问一个问题。这里的目标是弄清群体需要什么，不是说服所有人，也不是证明这次标签很准。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【MUM】人格。MUM 型人格最大的特点，就是无论走到哪里，都会自动长出一种“照顾全场”的功能。朋友发呆，您先问是不是累了；对象沉默，您先想是不是今天受委屈了；连刚认识的人打个喷嚏，您都想顺手把纸递过去。别人来人间是来体验生活，您来人间像是来担任临时生活后勤部长的。您并不一定刻意讨好，也不是见谁都想当妈，而是您真的很容易把别人装进自己的雷达范围。谁饿了、谁冷了、谁没台阶下、谁情绪快炸了，您常常比对方自己还先发现。您像人形托底系统，稳定、柔软、好使，还经常自带一句“没事，我来”。问题也在这里：您太会接别人了，于是有时候反而没人来接您。别人把您的靠谱当空气，把您的体贴当默认，您嘴上说“没关系”，心里其实也会偷偷累。MUM 人格的厉害之处，在于能用极温柔的方式把一屋子人的状态托住；难点则在于，别把自己托丢了。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew MUM. This character seems to acquire a ‘look after the whole room’ function wherever they go. A friend looks distracted, and MUM asks whether they are tired. A partner goes quiet, and MUM wonders whether the day has been difficult. Someone they have just met sneezes, and a tissue is already being offered. Other people arrive to experience life; MUM seems to arrive as the temporary head of practical support. The portrait does not require deliberate people-pleasing or wanting to be everyone's mother. Its central image is a wide interpersonal radar. Who is hungry, cold, embarrassed or close to an emotional overload? In the story, MUM often notices before the other person does. The character is a human back-up system: steady, gentle and ready with ‘It is all right; I will handle it.’ That creates the portrait's difficulty as well. Someone who catches everyone else can find that nobody catches them. Reliability becomes invisible, thoughtfulness becomes the default, and ‘It is fine’ may conceal growing tiredness. The original ending gives both sides of the joke: MUM can support a whole room with unusual gentleness, but must take care not to lose themselves while doing it. ‘Mom’ is the source's fictional profile name, not a conclusion about gender, parenthood or an obligation to provide care. The selected profile cannot establish that you know another person's needs without asking.

paragraphs.en: Imagine a friend becoming quieter during a gathering. You could assume they are upset, fill the silence for them or ask a simple question: “Would you like a break, company or neither?” The third approach leaves room for an answer you did not predict. The friend may be tired, absorbed in something else or simply enjoying listening.
paragraphs.zh: 比如聚会时，一位朋友逐渐安静。你可以猜对方不开心、替对方把沉默填满，也可以简单问：“想休息一下、有人陪着，还是都不用？”第三种问法，给没预料到的回答留了空间。朋友也可能只是累了、在想别的事，或正享受听别人说话。

paragraphs.en: Care can then mean accepting “I am fine” rather than escalating attention. In a shared task, the equivalent might be checking whether someone received the instructions, not deciding they need rescuing. What matters is the person’s stated need and the actual context; the quiz supplies neither of those facts.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，照应也可能意味着接受一句“我没事”，而不是继续加码关注。放到共同任务里，类似动作可能是确认对方收到说明没有，而不是认定对方需要被拯救。重要的是本人说出的需要和实际情境；游戏并不提供这两项事实。

paragraphs.en: A relevant check-in can make an invitation or a task easier to understand. Asking before offering advice may also reveal that listening is wanted instead of a solution. These are possible uses of a specific action, not abilities established by selecting a response in a quiz.
paragraphs.zh: 合适的确认，有时能让一次邀请或任务更容易被理解。给建议之前先问，也可能发现对方想要的是有人听，而不是一套解决方案。这是某项行动可能产生的用途，不是选了一个选项就证明的能力。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears if you become the default monitor of everyone’s comfort while your own needs go unspoken. It can also appear when an offer is hard to refuse. Check capacity and consent on both sides. Caring about a person does not create an unlimited obligation to be available, solve the problem or stay in an unsafe situation.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在你成了所有人舒适程度的默认监测员，自己的需要却一直没说；也可能出现在一个好意让人难以拒绝。可以同时核对双方的余力与意愿。在乎一个人，不会自动产生无限在线、解决问题或留在不安全处境里的义务。

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary interaction, make a small, specific offer and include a real way to decline. You might ask, “Would ten minutes of listening help, or would you rather have some quiet?” State what you can actually offer instead of promising unlimited support. The useful observation is what the person says and what happens next.
paragraphs.zh: 可以在一次普通互动里，提出一个小而具体、也真正能拒绝的帮助。比如：“听你说十分钟会有用吗，还是你更想安静一会儿？”说明自己实际能提供什么，而不是答应无限支持。值得观察的是对方怎么说，以及接下来实际发生了什么。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, check your own capacity as well. If the offer added more work than you could manage, change its scope next time. If the person preferred another kind of help, use that information rather than treating refusal as rejection of you. This is a bounded reflection, not a guarantee of better relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 事后也可以核对自己的余力。如果这个好意带来的工作超出承受范围，下次就缩小范围；如果对方更需要另一种帮助，可以使用这条信息，而不急着把拒绝理解为对自己的否定。这是有边界的观察，不保证关系一定改善。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【FAKE】人格。所谓“伪人”，并不是说您坏，也不是说您爱演，而是您对场景的适配能力高得有点不像人。见甲方一个版本，见朋友一个版本，见家里长辈一个版本，到了喜欢的人面前又自动切成另一个版本。别人换脸靠滤镜，您换脸靠生存本能。您不是没有真心，您只是很早就学会：在不同语境里，说最合适的话、摆最安全的姿势，往往比原样直出更有效。久而久之，您会发展出一种非常高级的能力，观察空气。空气一紧，您马上收；气氛一松，您立刻放；谁喜欢热闹，谁吃冷淡，谁要被照顾面子，谁要被给台阶，您看一眼就懂。别人觉得您会做人，您自己其实知道，这一套是练出来的。代价也很明显：切得太熟练了，有时连您自己都要愣一下，我现在这版，到底是不是我？答案通常是：都是。您不是没真我，您只是拥有一整个工具箱。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew FAKE. The original nickname plays with the idea of a ‘fake person’, but the story does not mean that you are bad or dishonest. Its character adapts to a setting with almost implausible speed. There is one version for a client, another for friends, another for older relatives, and another again around someone the character likes. Other people change faces with a filter; this character does it as a learned way of getting through life. The point is not an absence of sincere feelings. It is having learned that suitable words and a safer posture can work better in a particular situation than expressing everything without adjustment. Over time, the character develops a talent for ‘reading the air’. When tension rises, they pull back. When the atmosphere loosens, they relax. They notice who wants lively conversation, who prefers distance, who needs to save face and who needs an easier way out of an awkward exchange. Other people may call this social skill; the character knows how much practice it took. The cost comes when switching becomes so familiar that the character pauses to ask, ‘Is the version I am using now really me?’ The original answer is that these versions can all belong to the same person. The closing image is a whole toolbox rather than a missing true self. This is a playful portrait of changing expression, not evidence of deception, a diagnosis or a judgement about whether someone is a real person.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: Imagine asking for a later meeting time. With a close friend, you might simply say you need another hour. With a new colleague, you might explain the constraint and suggest alternatives. The wording changes, but the request can remain clear in both settings. Adapting expression does not require surrendering the request itself.
paragraphs.zh: 比如想把碰面时间往后挪一小时。对熟悉的朋友，你可能直接说还需要一小时；对新同事，你可能解释限制，再给出备选时间。说法变了，两种场合里的请求仍可以同样清楚。调整表达，不必等于放弃请求本身。

paragraphs.en: The relevant question is what the other person could actually understand. If the second version becomes so polite that nobody knows a change is needed, the adaptation has a cost. If it supplies useful context without hiding the request, it may fit this conversation. The quiz cannot tell which occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 可以核对的是：对方实际能听明白什么？如果第二种说法客气到没人知道需要改时间，调整就有了代价；如果增加的是有用背景，又没藏掉请求，它可能适合这次谈话。游戏无法判断当时是哪一种。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff is losing track of what you wanted to communicate while managing how it might be received. You might agree too quickly, postpone a necessary objection or spend a long time reviewing your performance. Those possibilities are prompts for a real example, not consequences established by a result.
paragraphs.zh: 需要取舍的地方，是忙着照顾话会怎样被接收，却慢慢忘了自己想表达什么。你可能答应太快、把必要的异议往后拖，或事后花很久复盘表现。这些只是可供核对的情境，不是结果已经证实的后果。

paragraphs.en: For an ordinary request, write one sentence stating what you mean before deciding how to say it. Then adapt the explanation for the listener. For example, keep “I cannot take this on this week” constant while changing the amount of background. The aim is clarity, not proving a type.
paragraphs.zh: 可以为一个普通请求先写一句“我到底是什么意思”，再决定怎样向对方解释。比如保留“这周我接不了这件事”，根据听众改变背景说明的多少。目的是让话更清楚，而不是证明自己属于哪一型。

paragraphs.en: After the conversation, compare the understood request with that original sentence. If they differ, a short clarification may be more useful than judging the whole interaction as a performance. If they match, you need not keep polishing it. This optional reflection does not promise confidence or social approval.
paragraphs.zh: 谈完后，可以比较对方理解到的请求和最初那句话。如果不同，一次简短澄清可能比把整场对话当表演评分更有用；如果一致，也不必一直打磨。这项可选观察不保证获得自信或他人好感。

paragraphs.zh: 动机和意义感维度偏低，整体更抽离。
paragraphs.en: This original portrait describes a more detached relationship to motivation and meaning.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了全中国最稀有的【DEAD】人格。请注意，这里的“死者”并不是字面意思，而是一种灵魂层面的“我看过了，我懂了，我不想再激动了”。别人还在为了目标、爱恨、成败、输赢、热搜、脸面和未来疯狂上头时，您已经像顶级玩家删档重开 999 次后一样，平静地对世界说：也就那样吧。不是没有兴趣，是兴趣被透支得差不多了。您看世界的眼神，像凌晨三点坐在窗边的 NPC：知道剧情、看穿套路、理解机制，但不太想参与。有人会觉得您丧、您冷、您像没电；其实您只是对很多“必须燃起来”的叙事免疫了。目标当然有过，热爱当然也不是没出现过，只是后来发现，很多东西追到头也未必会给人一个真正稳的答案。于是您逐渐修炼成一种高阶抽离：不再轻易被口号鼓动，不再轻易被别人的热情拖走。DEAD 人格不是废墟，是一种对过度意义生产的沉默抗议。别人活得像现场直播，您活得像幕后旁白。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: the original story jokingly introduces DEAD as an exceptionally rare profile. ‘Dead’ is not literal here. It is the character's weary ‘I have seen this, I understand it, and I do not feel like getting excited again.’ While others become absorbed in goals, affection, resentment, success, failure, public attention, reputation and the future, this character resembles an expert player who has restarted the same game 999 times and calmly says, ‘So that is how it is.’ The portrait is not simply an absence of interest; it imagines interest that has been spent too freely. The character watches the world like a background figure at a window at three in the morning: familiar with the plot, the routines and the mechanics, but not eager to join in. Other people may see gloom, coldness or a flat battery. The original story instead imagines someone no longer easily moved by demands to be enthusiastic. Goals and passions existed, but pursuing them did not always provide the lasting answer they seemed to promise. The character therefore becomes less easily pulled along by slogans or another person's excitement. DEAD ends as a quiet protest against producing too much meaning, rather than as a ruin. Others live as though broadcasting live; this character supplies the commentary from behind the scenes. The rarity and game language are original exaggerations. This result says nothing about death, depression, functioning or how rare a person is in the population.

paragraphs.en: Imagine being invited to an event because “everyone important will be there.” You are not immediately convinced. You might ask what will actually happen, whether you want those conversations and what attending would cost. Stepping back creates space to decide, but does not make attending shallow or declining wise.
paragraphs.zh: 比如有人邀你参加活动，理由是“重要的人都会去”。你没有马上被说服，想先问实际会发生什么、是否想进行那些交流，以及参加要付出什么。退一步可以给决定留空间，但不会使参加显得肤浅，或使拒绝自动显得明智。

paragraphs.en: Questioning a ready-made goal can help separate your own reasons from expectations you have inherited. The practical value lies in the reason you eventually identify, not in maintaining distance for its own sake. This guide does not claim that detachment produces clearer judgment or a superior perspective.
paragraphs.zh: 问一问现成目标，可以帮助区分自己的理由和接过来的期待。实际价值在于最后辨认出了什么理由，而不是为了抽离而保持抽离。这份指南不声称距离会带来更清晰的判断或更优越的视角。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff can appear if every possible activity is dismissed before you learn enough to choose. Some useful experiences begin without a grand purpose. You can inspect one small opportunity without committing to its whole story. Whether that is worthwhile depends on your circumstances, not on a theme result.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在还没了解多少，就把每个活动都否定的时候。有些有用体验并不以宏大意义开场。你可以只看看一个小机会，不必连它的整套叙事都接受。值不值得，取决于现实处境，而不是主题结果。

paragraphs.en: Choose an ordinary invitation or task and complete two sentences: “The reason offered to me is…” and “My reason for joining or declining is….” They may match. If they do not, you can keep the distinction without deciding that either side is foolish. No big statement about your purpose is required.
paragraphs.zh: 可以选一项普通邀请或任务，补完两句话：“别人给出的理由是……”以及“我参加或拒绝的理由是……”。两者可以相同；不同的时候，也可以保留差别，不必先判断哪一方愚蠢。这里不需要给自己的人生目标作大声明。

paragraphs.en: If you are unsure, identify one piece of information or one limited experience that could help. You can also decline without performing an experiment. The purpose is to make a real choice more legible, not to prove you are detached or force yourself to become enthusiastic.

paragraphs.en: I have not disappeared. I have switched to offline power-saving mode.

paragraphs.zh: 关系和行动维度波动较大，回避倾向偏明显。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait describes variable engagement in relationships and action, with a tendency to step away.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【ZZZZ】人格。装死者的伟大之处，在于把“暂时不回应”发展成了一门带有东方神秘主义色彩的高阶技能。群里 99+ 消息，您可以视而不见；日程排山倒海地压过来，您也能先把自己折起来；别人越急，您越想先静一静，像一只自动钻进洞里的谨慎生物。您不是不负责，也不是故意冷暴力，您只是非常懂得：当电量不足时，强行运行只会死机。有趣的是，您虽然平时像休眠仓里的神秘乘客，但一旦“死线”二字出现，您又会像古墓开棺般缓缓苏醒，先发一个“收到”，再在最后时刻交出一份勉强及格甚至突然惊艳的成果。您向宇宙证明了一个朴素真理：有时候什么都不做，就不会做错；但真到必须动的时候，您也并不是一点都不行。ZZZZ 人格的核心不是懒，而是能量管理极端依赖感觉。您像一台老旧但可靠的机器：平时省电、偶尔沉睡、关键时刻会响，然后一响惊人。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew ZZZZ. The character turns temporarily not responding into an almost mystical advanced skill. A group chat has more than 99 messages? They can leave it unread. A mountain of appointments arrives? They can fold themselves away first. The more urgently others move, the more this cautious creature wants to retreat into a quiet hole. The original story does not call this irresponsibility or deliberate emotional punishment. It imagines someone who knows that forcing a low battery to keep running can make the system crash. Like an ancient chamber slowly opening, the character wakes, sends a short acknowledgement and produces something just good enough at the last moment, or perhaps unexpectedly impressive. The joke offers two apparently conflicting truths: sometimes doing nothing avoids doing something wrong, but when movement is unavoidable, the character is not wholly incapable of moving. ZZZZ is described less as laziness than as energy management that relies heavily on how things feel. The closing image is an old but dependable machine: saving power much of the time, occasionally sleeping, then making a surprising noise when the critical moment arrives. This is the original humorous portrait of withdrawal and last-minute movement, not evidence that withdrawing from someone is harmless or that deadlines always produce a good outcome.

paragraphs.en: Imagine several messages arriving while you are finishing a demanding task. You want to step away from the conversation. In the original joke, this gives physical form to the sentence, ‘I really do have an opinion about this.’ While others work out how to express themselves politely, the character's immediate reaction pushes through like weeds through a crack in concrete. The portrait does not imagine someone deliberately opposing everyone or planning to disrupt every room. It describes reluctance to polish a reaction into a version that feels safe to others but stifling to oneself. Something objectionable produces a frown. An uncomfortable interaction produces distance. When a firm reply seems necessary, the character rarely applies an emotional beauty filter first. The final image is spring grass growing with an almost unruly liveliness: quick, wild and somewhat unconcerned with approval. If called too confrontational, the imagined answer is, ‘I just do not have time to perform.’ This is an exaggerated entertainment voice, not permission to insult, intimidate or disregard another person's boundaries. paragraphs.en: Imagine someone asking for another task when your afternoon is already committed. “I cannot finish both today; which should take priority?” names a constraint and opens a practical question. paragraphs.en: The answer may reveal a misunderstanding, an urgent need or a workload problem. You may still disagree after hearing it. A meaningful next step could be clarifying the arrangement or ending the discussion, depending on the context. The quiz cannot determine a real obligation or whether a setting is safe.

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when urgency in your delivery obscures the actual request or leaves no room for another person’s answer. That does not remove your right to refuse. You can separate the boundary from the way it was conveyed, and decide whether clarification is useful without withdrawing a legitimate limit.
paragraphs.zh: 需要取舍的地方，是表达里的急迫盖住了实际请求，或不给对方回答的空间。这不会取消你拒绝的权利。可以把界限本身和表达方式分开，判断是否需要澄清，而不必因此收回合理限制。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, check whether the actual constraint became clearer. If the problem persists because responsibility or workload is unclear, address that issue rather than treating your delivery as the entire cause. paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【CTRL】人格。CTRL 型人格的核心诉求很简单：事情最好在可控范围内，人也最好别给我突然掉线。您不一定非要站在正中央，但至少要知道现在发生了什么、接下来可能出什么岔子，以及最坏情况来了要往哪儿拐。别人把随机性当生活情趣，您把随机性当事故源头。别人追求惊喜，您更喜欢“我早就知道会这样”。您很擅长做风险预判，也很擅长留后手。Plan A、Plan B、Plan C 不是您故意复杂，而是您的安全感本来就建立在“我心里有数”之上。您看起来很会控场、很会拿捏、很有分寸，本质上是因为您太不喜欢把自己交给混乱。您甚至连别人的情绪走向、关系升温、场面冷掉都想顺手管一管。CTRL 人格的可怕之处，在于它并不总是高调，而是安安静静地把一切都调到了自己能接受的频率。别人说您会拿捏，您心想：不拿捏，难道等着被局面拿捏吗？
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew CTRL. This character's central wish is simple: events should remain within a manageable range, and people should not suddenly disappear from the plan. The character does not always need to stand in the middle of the room, but wants to know what is happening, what might go wrong next and which direction to turn if the worst happens. Where someone else treats unpredictability as the spice of life, CTRL sees a possible incident. Where someone else wants a surprise, this character prefers being able to say, ‘I knew that would happen.’ The original portrait places risk anticipation and back-up plans at its centre. Plans A, B and C are not complexity for its own sake; knowing what is going on becomes a source of reassurance. What looks like control, influence or careful judgement grows out of a dislike of handing oneself over to chaos. In the exaggerated story, even another person's changing mood, a relationship becoming warmer or a room falling silent can invite an attempt to manage the situation. CTRL does not always do this loudly. The character may quietly adjust the surroundings until they feel bearable. The closing comeback is, ‘If I do not get a handle on the situation, am I supposed to let the situation get a handle on me?’ This story does not establish that predictions are accurate or that directing another person is appropriate.

paragraphs.en: Imagine a shared trip whose departure time changes. You check who will tell the others, whether a connection still works and what happens if it does not. paragraphs.zh: 比如一次共同出行的出发时间改变了。你想确认谁来通知其他人、后面的衔接是否还行，以及不行时怎么办。这些是具体依赖，与替所有人安排感受，或要求任何人都不能改变偏好，不是一回事。

paragraphs.en: A short check may resolve the issue; a longer plan may add little. The relevant question is what uncertainty has a practical consequence. If you cannot identify one, it may be enough to agree on an update and leave the rest open. The result cannot determine that boundary for you.

paragraphs.en: A relevant backup can make a dependency visible and give people a shared next step. Check whether it is understandable, feasible and agreed. The act of planning is not itself proof of safety, reliability or good judgment, and another person may see a constraint your plan missed.
paragraphs.zh: 相关的备选办法可以让依赖关系可见，也给大家一个共同的下一步。可以核对它是否清楚、可行，并得到同意。做了计划，本身不证明安全、可靠或判断良好；别人也可能看见计划漏掉的限制。

paragraphs.en: The tradeoff appears when each answer generates another condition without changing the decision. A checklist can also become a way to direct people who never accepted that arrangement. Separate what needs agreement from what you would merely prefer, and allow the plan to change when new information makes it less useful.
paragraphs.zh: 取舍可能出现在每个答案又引出一个条件，却始终不改变决定的时候。清单也可能变成指挥那些从未同意该安排的人的办法。可以区分必须达成共识的事和自己的偏好；新信息使计划不再适用时，也允许它改变。

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes plan, identify a dependency, who needs the information and one fallback. For example: “If the room is unavailable, we will use this alternative; I will confirm it by noon.” Keep the proposal small enough for everyone affected to understand and question.
paragraphs.zh: 可以在一个低风险计划中，找一项依赖、需要知道信息的人，以及一个备选办法。比如：“如果房间不能用，就换这个地点；中午前由我确认。”把提案保持在受影响的人都能理解、也能提出疑问的范围里。

paragraphs.en: After using it, ask whether the fallback changed anything useful or simply added work. If it was unnecessary, reduce it next time. If a missing agreement was the real issue, address that rather than creating more checklists. This optional reflection does not promise better outcomes or eliminate uncertainty.

paragraphs.zh: 情绪缓冲能力较高，轻松感更显著。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【HHHH】人格。傻乐者不是傻，重点在“乐”。您像那种生活里自带缓冲棉的人，很多别人马上会紧起来的事，到了您这里会先被乐子感过滤一遍。现场尴尬？先哈哈。计划翻车？先哈哈。自己倒霉？也能先哈哈两声再说。别人觉得您没心没肺，您其实只是懂得：人类如果什么都认真到骨头里，那很快就会提前报废。您并不是不痛，也不是看不懂沉重，而是知道很多事认真半天也未必能立刻改变，不如先给自己留口气。您像生活的自救浮板，情绪来了先把自己托住，别急着沉。您身边的人也常常会被这种能力传染：本来快要窒息的气氛，被您一句轻描淡写的玩笑就缓过来了。傻乐者最厉害的地方，不是永远快乐，而是在一地鸡毛里还能找出一点能笑的东西。别人靠鸡汤活，您靠哈哈哈续命。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew HHHH. The point of the Chinese nickname is not stupidity but laughter. This character seems to carry a layer of cushioning through everyday life. Things that make someone else tense are first passed through a search for something amusing. An awkward silence? A laugh. A plan falls apart? Another laugh. The character has bad luck? There may still be two laughs available. Other people can mistake this for having no worries, but the original portrait imagines someone who knows that taking every event to the deepest possible level would wear a person out early. The character can feel pain and understand seriousness. The story's argument is simply that prolonged seriousness does not always change a situation immediately, so a little breathing room may help. HHHH becomes a small flotation device: when feelings arrive, stay afloat before sinking. The atmosphere around other people can change too. A room that felt difficult to breathe in may loosen after one lightly delivered joke. The portrait's strength is not being happy at every moment; it is finding something that permits laughter among the small disasters of ordinary life. Where another character might live on inspirational speeches, HHHH lives on another ‘ha ha ha’. The result is an entertainment portrait, not evidence that humour resolves a problem or that another person should stop taking their feelings seriously.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: Two friends take the wrong exit and have to walk back. Once they know the route is safe, one notices a ridiculous shop sign and shares a laugh. The fun can sit beside the practical correction: checking directions and deciding whether both people still want to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 两个朋友走错出口，需要折返。确认路线安全后，其中一人注意到一块好笑的店招，分享了这个细节。乐趣可以与实际补救并存：核对方向，再问两个人是否仍愿意继续。

paragraphs.en: If the other person is exhausted or upset, a joke may not be helpful. Asking what they need can matter more than keeping the mood light. The label gives no reason to minimize an inconvenience, mock someone, or treat a serious concern as entertainment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果对方已经疲惫或难受，玩笑可能没有帮助。问问需要什么，可以比活跃气氛更重要。标签不能成为淡化麻烦、嘲笑别人或把严肃困扰当娱乐的理由。

paragraphs.en: A small playful suggestion may make an ordinary activity more enjoyable when everyone welcomes it. Whether that happens depends on timing and the people involved. The result does not establish social skill, resilience or the ability to make a group comfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 大家都欢迎时，一点玩乐提议可能让普通活动更有趣；是否如此，取决于时机与参与者。结果不能确定社交技巧、韧性或让集体舒服的能力。

paragraphs.en: Trying to lighten every moment can leave less room for disappointment or disagreement. Notice whether you are enjoying the exchange or feeling responsible for everyone’s mood. You can let a silence remain and still be a considerate participant.
paragraphs.zh: 如果每一刻都急着缓和，失望或分歧可能没机会说完。可以留意自己是在享受互动，还是觉得必须负责所有人的心情。让一段沉默留在那里，也可以是体贴的参与方式。

paragraphs.en: If you want an experiment, suggest one harmless addition to a routine activity: choosing a silly name for a shared shopping list, for example. Ask whether the other person wants to join in. A plain “not today” is enough to end the experiment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果想试一试，可以给日常活动提一个无害小点子，例如给共同购物清单取个好玩的名字。先问别人是否愿意参与；一句“今天不想”就足够结束尝试。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, recall the actual response rather than whether it matched your label. You may prefer a different tone next time. No exercise is necessary to complete the guide, and you do not need to laugh at yourself or reveal an embarrassing story.
paragraphs.zh: 之后回想真实回应，而不是有没有符合标签。下次你可以选择另一种语气。不做练习也能读完指南，更不必拿自己开玩笑或公开出糗经历。

paragraphs.zh: 你往那一站，空气都会自动调成柔焦。
paragraphs.en: Stand there and the air seems to switch to soft focus.

paragraphs.zh: 外显魅力和氛围感维度更高，辨识度强。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait emphasises a noticeable presence, expressive appeal and atmosphere.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【SEXY】人格。所谓尤物，不一定是教科书意义上的浓颜大美人，也不一定是标准模板里的“性感”。您更像一种会自动聚光的气场：站在人群里，很容易被看到；说一句话，氛围会自己发生变化；哪怕什么都不做，也有一种“这人很有画面”的存在感。别人靠补光灯，您靠自身磁场。SEXY 人格往往很懂氛围，也很懂分寸。您知道什么时候该收，什么时候该放，什么时候一个眼神就够，什么时候一句话就能把现场气温抬高两度。别人会说您“很会”，但您不一定是刻意经营的，因为这种吸引力很多时候是天然的，来自气质、来自表达、来自审美、来自对自己身体和存在感的直觉。您不是每时每刻都在发光，但您有一种让人记住的能力：别人走了只剩背影，您走了还能留下余温。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew SEXY. The original portrait does not require someone to look like a textbook beauty or fit a standard template of being sexy. It imagines a presence that draws a spotlight. The character is easily noticed in a crowd; a sentence can change the atmosphere, and even doing nothing can create a memorable image. Where someone else needs a lighting rig, this character supposedly has a personal magnetic field. In the story, SEXY understands atmosphere and restraint together: when to hold back, when to open up, when a look is enough and when a sentence can make the room feel two degrees warmer. Other people may say the character knows exactly what they are doing, but the portrait does not necessarily imagine a carefully managed performance. It locates the appeal in manner, expression, aesthetic choices and an intuitive sense of one's own physical presence. The character need not shine at every moment. The closing image is simply being remembered: someone else leaves a silhouette behind, while this character seems to leave warmth in the room. This is the original flattering, exaggerated entertainment portrait. The result cannot measure attractiveness, someone else's interest, social influence or consent. Eye-Catcher is the source's softer display name; SEXY remains the original profile code.

paragraphs.zh: 情感投入度：你投入情绪时会带着氛围感，别人很容易感觉到你的存在温度。
paragraphs.en: Emotional investment: Your emotional engagement carries a sense of atmosphere, making your presence easy for others to feel.

paragraphs.zh: 边界与依赖：你对边界和依赖的拿捏，不会一路失控，也不会完全无感。
paragraphs.en: Boundaries and dependence: Your approach to boundaries and dependence is neither continually out of control nor entirely detached.

paragraphs.zh: 世界观倾向：你看世界时既会带入感受，也会保留一点自己的判断。
paragraphs.en: View of the world: You bring feelings into your view of the world while retaining some judgement of your own.

paragraphs.zh: 规则与灵活度：你对规则不是死守，也不是彻底摆烂，更多是按场景调节。
paragraphs.en: Rules and flexibility: You neither follow rules rigidly nor abandon them entirely; you tend to adjust to the situation.

paragraphs.zh: 人生意义感：你会想人为什么这样活着，但还不至于天天把自己想进死胡同。
paragraphs.en: Life and meaning: You think about why people live as they do without necessarily thinking yourself into a dead end every day.

paragraphs.zh: 动机导向：你有自己的动机来源，只是发力方式不总是同一种。
paragraphs.en: Sources of motivation: You have sources of motivation of your own, but they do not always express themselves in the same way.

paragraphs.zh: 决策风格：你做决定时会混合理性、直觉和当下状态，不算单线程。
paragraphs.en: Decision style: Your decisions mix reasoning, intuition and your present state rather than following a single track.

paragraphs.zh: 执行模式：你推进事情的方式有弹性，能冲也能缓，不是一种节奏打天下。
paragraphs.en: Way of acting: Your way of moving things forward is flexible: sometimes you push and sometimes you slow down.

paragraphs.zh: 社交主动性：你在社交场里有天然存在感，不用太用力也能被注意到。
paragraphs.en: Social initiative: You have a noticeable presence in social settings without necessarily making a great effort.

paragraphs.zh: 人际边界感：你的人际边界感基本在线，知道什么时候靠近、什么时候退开。
paragraphs.en: Interpersonal boundaries: You generally have a sense of interpersonal boundaries and know when to approach or step back.

paragraphs.zh: 表达与真实度：你的表达真实度会混着风格感一起出来，辨识度比较高。
paragraphs.en: Authentic expression: Your genuine expression comes with a recognisable personal style.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: You invite friends to a meal and enjoy choosing a small drawing or a characteristic phrase for the message. The detail helps the invitation feel yours. Whether the meal is pleasant still depends on practical arrangements and the people attending, not on the design alone.
paragraphs.zh: 邀请朋友吃饭时，你喜欢给消息选一个小图案或一句带个人味道的话。细节让邀请更像自己；饭局是否愉快，仍取决于实际安排与参与者，不由设计单独决定。

paragraphs.en: A clear, plain message can serve the same purpose. Someone who spends no time on styling may care deeply about the gathering. The contrast in the questionnaire is about what feels more familiar to you, never which person makes a better friend.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚朴素的消息也能达到目的。完全不做造型的人，也可能十分在乎聚会。题中比较的是哪种描述更熟悉，不是谁更适合当朋友。

paragraphs.en: Preparation can become tiring when every message or appearance feels like a test. Consider which details you enjoy and which you feel pressured to maintain. You may simplify, repeat an outfit or leave something unfinished without contradicting a supposed identity.
paragraphs.zh: 每条消息或每次露面都像考试时，准备会变累。可以分清哪些细节自己喜欢，哪些是觉得必须维持。简化、重复穿着或暂留未完成，都不违背什么固定身份。

paragraphs.en: If useful, choose one low-cost detail in an ordinary activity: a color in a personal note or a phrase in a message. Ask what you like about it before considering anyone else’s reaction. You can keep the activity private and need not buy or post anything.
paragraphs.zh: 如果觉得有用，可以在普通小事中选一个无需额外花费的细节，例如私人笔记的颜色或消息里一句话。先问自己喜欢什么，再考虑他人反应。可以完全私下完成，无需购买或发布。

title.zh: 无所谓人（OJBK）SBTI原31题结果解读

summary.zh: 情绪起伏不算高，抽离和松弛感更明显。
summary.en: The original portrait describes smaller emotional swings, detachment and an easier pace.

scoreReading.zh: 这是原31题玩法中的一个趣味画像；实际提交后展示原结果代码及15维模型数字。
scoreReading.en: This is one playful portrait from the original 31-question edition. Completing it shows the original result code and fifteen model numbers.

paragraphs.zh: 也行，都行，差不多得了。
paragraphs.en: That works. Anything works. Good enough will do.

paragraphs.zh: 情绪起伏不算高，抽离和松弛感更明显。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait describes smaller emotional swings, detachment and an easier pace.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【OJBK】人格。无所谓人不是没有态度，而是对很多事情的态度都相当稳定：没必要太较真。别人对一个座位、一个输赢、一个小细节耿耿于怀时，您大概率会在旁边淡淡来一句：“行吧，也不是不行。”您不是绝对佛，也不是完全没追求，只是您非常清楚：人类每天需要较真的事情已经够多了，没必要把自己所有精力都耗在鸡毛蒜皮上。OJBK 最大的优势，就是松。别人卷得像要发射火箭，您可以默默坐在旁边喝水；别人因为一点风吹草动情绪翻车，您通常也能给自己留出缓冲空间。您对外界节奏有天然的抽离感，不是进不去，而是懒得每次都全力投入。您未必是赢面最大的人，但通常也不是输得最惨的那个。因为您天生懂得一个简单道理：很多事如果不把它当成天塌了，它就真的塌不下来。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew OJBK. This character is not without an attitude. Rather, the attitude towards many things stays fairly consistent: there is no need to take every detail so seriously. While someone else dwells on a seat, a small win or loss, or a minor point, this character may quietly say, ‘All right. It is not impossible.’ The original portrait does not describe perfect serenity or an absence of ambition. It imagines someone who recognises that life already supplies enough matters requiring effort, without spending every remaining bit of energy on trivia. The profile's main feature is looseness. While others strain as though launching a rocket, the character can sit nearby drinking water. When a small disturbance knocks another person's feelings off course, OJBK tends to leave a little room for cushioning. The character is somewhat detached from the pace around them: not unable to join in, but reluctant to invest maximum effort every single time. The original story allows that this person may not have the greatest chance of winning, yet may also avoid the worst possible loss. Its final joke is that many events cease to feel like the sky falling if they are not treated as the sky falling. This portrait is not evidence that consequences disappear, that every compromise is acceptable or that another person's concern is trivial.

title.zh: 补充情境：把画像放回日常
title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: A friend suggests two nearby cafés. Both fit your budget and access needs, and you genuinely have no strong preference. Letting the friend choose can be a complete decision. You need not invent a stronger preference to appear engaged.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友提出附近两家咖啡馆，都符合你的预算和出入需要，你也确实没有强烈偏好。让朋友选，可以是完整决定；不必为了显得投入，刻意制造一个更强烈的偏好。

paragraphs.en: If one café is inaccessible, too expensive or uncomfortable for you, the choice is no longer neutral. Saying so gives the other person useful information. Going along despite an important unmet need is a different situation from the low-stakes descriptions here.
paragraphs.zh: 如果一家出入不便、太贵或让你不舒服，选择就不再中性。说出来能给对方有用信息。重要需求未被满足却仍勉强顺从，与本页描述的低风险随和是不同情境。

paragraphs.en: If “anything is fine” becomes your automatic response, others may not know when something matters. You can say, “Either time works, but I do need to leave by six.” Flexibility and an explicit limit can coexist without becoming opposite personality types.
paragraphs.zh: 如果“都行”成了自动回答，别人可能不知道什么对你重要。可以说“两个时间都可以，但我六点前需要离开”。灵活与明确限制可以并存，无需归为相反人格。

paragraphs.en: For one ordinary plan, identify an acceptable range before replying. You might name two workable times and one real limit. Then let the other person choose within that range. This is an optional communication experiment, not an instruction to become more accommodating.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一项普通安排，可以先找出能接受的范围再回复。例如给出两个可行时间，再说明一个真实限制，让对方在范围内选。这只是可选沟通尝试，不要求变得更加迁就。

paragraphs.zh: 我的人生预算表里，安全感永远最贵。
paragraphs.en: In my life's budget, a sense of security is always the most expensive item.

paragraphs.zh: 资源感知更强，安全感经常和现实条件绑定。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait connects sensitivity to resources with practical conditions and security.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【POOR】人格。贫穷者并不只是钱包的状态，更是一种对“资源够不够”的超高敏感雷达。钱够不够，时间够不够，精力够不够，人情够不够，明天顶不顶得住，别人还在凭感觉活，您已经默默在脑内做完一轮资产负债表。您不是现实，是您太知道现实会在什么时候给人一闷棍。您对生活有很强的成本意识，也因此显得谨慎、克制、偶尔甚至有点抠搜。可说到底，这不是因为您不想大方，而是因为您太清楚：很多热血和浪漫，最后都要靠具体资源来买单。别人用“冲动消费”证明活着，您用“先算一下”确保明天还能活。贫穷者人格的厉害，不在于多会享受，而在于哪怕资源有限，也会一边咬牙一边继续把日子撑住。您不是不想松，是现实总提醒您先别松。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew POOR. The original character is not simply a description of a wallet. It is an unusually sensitive radar for whether there will be enough resources. Enough money, time, energy, goodwill: will tomorrow hold together? While someone else follows a feeling, the character has quietly completed a balance sheet in their head. The story does not present this as merely being hard-headed. It imagines someone who knows when practical reality can land a blow. Awareness of cost can look cautious, restrained and occasionally rather tight-fisted. Yet the portrait's explanation is not a lack of generosity: it is knowing that enthusiasm and romance eventually have to be supported by concrete resources. Where someone else uses an impulsive purchase to feel alive, this character first does the arithmetic to make sure tomorrow remains possible. The original strength is not exceptional enjoyment or luxury. It is continuing to hold ordinary life together, sometimes through gritted teeth, when resources are limited. The closing thought is not that the character never wants to relax, but that circumstances keep reminding them to wait. Budget-Strained is the source's softer display name. Receiving the original POOR code does not reveal income, wealth, debt, class or financial hardship, and the profile should not be used to judge those circumstances.

paragraphs.en: A weekly class looks enjoyable, but attendance would also require travel and preparation. You check the whole commitment rather than the first session alone. You might choose a shorter course, decline for now or decide the continuing cost is acceptable.

paragraphs.en: None of those outcomes follows from the theme label. A person can review resources carefully and still choose an expensive experience. Likewise, declining can reflect a hard constraint rather than a stable preference for caution.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果都不是标签规定的。认真核对资源后，也可以选择花费较大的体验；拒绝也可能来自硬性限制，而不是稳定的谨慎偏好。

paragraphs.en: Checking continuing demands can make a hidden tradeoff visible. Whether it helps depends on the information available and what matters to you. The questionnaire cannot determine an affordable amount, a correct budget or whether a purchase is worthwhile.

paragraphs.en: Repeatedly reviewing a small expense may itself use attention. Notice whether you need another fact or simply permission to choose within your own limits. Enjoyment is a legitimate consideration; the theme is not a moral ranking of saving over spending.
paragraphs.zh: 反复核对一笔小开销，本身也会占用注意力。可以留意自己是缺一条信息，还是需要允许自己在限度内作决定。乐趣也是合理考虑；本主题不把节省排在花费之上作道德评价。

paragraphs.en: For an ordinary optional plan, list its immediate demand and one continuing demand. Choose a limit that belongs to you, such as one evening or a fixed amount of preparation. You need not disclose financial or personal details to anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一项可选普通安排，写下即时要求与一项后续要求，再给自己定一个限度，例如一个晚上或固定准备时长。不必向任何人披露财务或私人细节。

paragraphs.zh: 可以据此作具体回复：“我能帮这一个小时，但不能接下整件事。”之后再看实际结果。练习可以不做，也不提供财务、就业或照护管理建议。

paragraphs.en: Other people see possibilities. You see where the wheels could come off.

paragraphs.zh: 负面预判更快，风险雷达更灵。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait emphasises quick anticipation of unwanted outcomes and an active risk radar.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【OH-NO】人格。您最大的天赋，不是乐观，而是预警。别人刚开始兴奋，您已经开始想这事会不会出 bug；别人说“应该没问题”，您脑内已经连续播放三版最坏结局。您不是天生扫兴，也不一定是悲观主义哲学家，您只是风险雷达开得特别早、特别响、特别不肯下班。世界在您眼里，永远带着一点“哦不，这不会又要出事吧”的熟悉底色。这种人格看起来有点累，但也确实管用。很多人因为太敢冲而反复摔跤，而您虽然紧绷，却常常能提前绕开坑。您对关系、计划、突发状况和微妙气氛都格外敏锐，别人还在傻乐时，您可能已经闻到了空气里一丝不对劲。OH-NO 人格不是唱衰，而是一种高频预警机制：您嘴里的“哦不”，其实是在替未来的自己提前报警。别人笑您想太多，您只会安静地记下：等下翻车了你别来找我。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew OH-NO. The character's special talent in the original story is not optimism but early warning. Just as someone else becomes excited, the character starts wondering where a bug might appear. Someone says it should be fine, and three versions of the worst ending are already playing in the character's mind. The portrait does not necessarily mean someone is deliberately spoiling the atmosphere or subscribes to a pessimistic philosophy. It imagines a risk radar that turns on early, sounds loudly and refuses to finish its shift. The world acquires a familiar background question: ‘Oh no, is something about to happen again?’ This looks tiring, but the original story also gives it a practical side. Where repeated bold charges can end in a fall, this tense character may sometimes notice a pit early enough to go around it. Relationships, plans, unexpected events and small changes of atmosphere all draw attention. While someone else is still laughing, OH-NO may already think something feels slightly wrong. The final metaphor is a high-frequency warning system sounding an alarm for the future self. If told they worry too much, the imagined private reply is, ‘If this falls apart later, do not come running to me.’ This is a comic portrait, not evidence that warnings are accurate, that a bad outcome is likely or that the result identifies an anxiety condition.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: A group is excited about an event and starts arranging transport. You notice that the date came from an old message and ask someone to confirm it. The useful part is the checkable question: which date is current and where can it be verified?
paragraphs.zh: 大家兴奋地准备活动，开始安排交通。你注意到日期来自旧消息，便请人确认。有用之处是可核实的问题：现在到底是哪天，能到哪里查证？

paragraphs.en: The date may turn out to be correct. Raising a concern does not make it a prediction that must come true. Nor does one correct concern prove that every worry deserves the same response; the evidence and practical consequence still need attention.
paragraphs.zh: 日期也可能本来就正确。提出疑问不等于作出了必须应验的预测；一次疑问正确，也不证明每份担心都应得到相同回应，仍需看证据与实际后果。

paragraphs.en: An early question may uncover a missing dependency before people commit. It can also interrupt momentum when the concern is too vague to investigate. The game cannot decide which happened; notice whether you identified a specific uncertainty and a proportionate way to check it.
paragraphs.zh: 早一点的问题可能在投入前发现遗漏条件；太模糊、无从调查的担忧也可能打断进展。游戏不能判定是哪种情况，可以看自己是否指出具体未知，以及相称的核对办法。

paragraphs.en: Some uncertainty remains after reasonable checking. You do not need certainty about everything to make an ordinary decision. If a concern persists, distinguish what you can verify, what someone else owns and what you can simply leave unresolved.
paragraphs.zh: 合理核对后仍会有不确定性。普通决定不要求先对一切确定。担忧持续时，可以区分自己能查什么、什么由别人负责，以及什么可以暂时不解决。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, notice whether the check changed the plan or merely reassured you temporarily. Either observation can guide a later choice. You need not repeat the exercise, and it is not a treatment for persistent worry or a substitute for safety procedures.
paragraphs.zh: 之后注意核对是否改变了计划，还是仅暂时安心。两种观察都可供下次参考。不必反复练习；它不治疗持续担忧，也不代替安全规程。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【MONK】人格。僧人型人格最大的魅力，就是对很多让普通人上头的东西天然免疫。不是完全没有欲望，而是那种“非要得到不可”的劲，在您身上不太常见。名利、热闹、攀比、过度亲密、激烈情绪，这些在人群里疯狂搅动的东西，到了您这里像是被自动调低了音量。别人忙着争抢和纠缠，您像坐在一旁的旁听僧，偶尔抬眼看一眼，心里想：就这？这并不意味着您永远快乐，或者对世界毫无兴趣。您只是比大多数人更擅长和自己待在一起，也更擅长在热闹边缘保持清醒。很多人活得像被欲望驱赶的兽群，您更像一个已经知道自己不需要所有东西的人。MONK 人格的强，不在于赢很多，而在于不容易被拖着走；不在于占有很多，而在于失去一点也不至于崩。别人靠刺激确认自己还活着，您靠安静确认自己没丢。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew MONK. The character's appeal in the original story is an apparent immunity to many things that make other people intensely excited. This is not complete freedom from desire. It is a smaller amount of ‘I absolutely have to obtain that.’ Fame, money, noise, comparison, excessive closeness and intense feelings seem to have their volume automatically lowered around this character. While others compete or become tangled up, MONK sits nearby like a quiet observer, looks up occasionally and wonders, ‘Is that all?’ The portrait does not promise permanent happiness or an absence of interest in the world. It imagines someone comfortable spending time with themselves and staying alert at the edge of a lively gathering. Where others look as though desire is driving them forward, this character appears to know they do not need everything on offer. The original strength is not winning a great deal but being less easily pulled along; not possessing a great deal but remaining intact when something is lost. The closing comparison is between confirming one's existence through stimulation and checking through quietness that one has not lost oneself. Monk is a fictional profile name. The selected result does not establish religious identity, sexual or romantic identity, emotional stability, virtue or superiority, and wanting something intensely does not make another person a lesser character.

paragraphs.en: The original portrait combines frustration, disorder and growing exasperation with practical responsibility.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了宇宙中已知的唯一一种【SHIT】人格。所谓狗屎，不是单纯在抱怨，而是一种把崩溃、无语、烦躁和责任感同时混合后，压缩发酵成的高级人类形态。您的嘴上常年挂着“这事真他妈离谱”“这项目真是一坨”“这人怎么能这样”，但手上并不会闲着。别人边骂边摆，您边骂边救；别人边崩边躺，您边崩边把 Excel 打开继续做。嘴上是一座垃圾填埋场，行动上却像凌晨四点还在补锅的城市维护系统。SHIT 人格最离谱的地方在于：您明明每天都像在和这个世界绝交，却又总能在关键时刻把它从坑里往外捞一点。您对混乱不陌生，对荒谬也没幻想，甚至已经形成了一套黑色幽默式的生存哲学：世界就是这样一坨，但活还是得干，锅还是得背，明天还是得起床挤地铁。别人可能以为您满身戾气，实际上那更像是一种燃料，如果不吐槽，不骂两句，您根本没法把这些破事继续扛下去。别怕，您嘴里的“屎”，未必是末日警报，也可能只是开工前的鸣笛。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: the original joke calls SHIT the only known personality of its kind in the universe. This is not merely a character who complains. It mixes feeling overwhelmed, speechlessness, irritation and responsibility into a compact, fermented human form. The character says, ‘This is ridiculous,’ ‘This project is a mess,’ or ‘How can someone act like that?’ Yet the hands do not stop working. Someone else complains and gives up; this character complains and rescues the situation. Someone else collapses on the sofa; this character opens a spreadsheet while falling apart. The mouth resembles a rubbish tip, but the actions resemble a city maintenance team still repairing things at four in the morning. The most absurd part of the portrait is declaring a break with the world every day, then helping pull it out of a hole at the important moment. Chaos is familiar, and absurdity is no surprise. A darkly comic philosophy has developed: the world may be a mess, but work still needs doing, responsibility still lands somewhere, and tomorrow still includes getting up for the train. What sounds like constant hostility can function in the story as fuel. Complaining makes continuing possible. The closing joke is that the swear word may not be a warning of the apocalypse; it may just be the whistle before a shift begins. These are fictional exaggerations, not a diagnosis or a reason to accept unmanageable responsibilities.

paragraphs.en: If you quietly check every category after agreeing to only one, others may not see the extra effort or know what needs changing. A practical correction can be useful without creating a standing obligation to fix the same problem every time.
paragraphs.zh: 如果只答应一个类别，却默默核对全部，别人可能看不见额外投入，也不知道哪里需要改变。一次实际补救可以有用，但不会自动形成以后每次都要补位的义务。

paragraphs.en: Naming a problem while contributing may make both your concern and your available help clearer. That is a possible outcome, not a skill proven by the result. Timing, wording and the other people’s willingness to respond all affect what happens.
paragraphs.zh: 一边提出问题一边投入，可能让关切与可提供的帮助都更清楚。这只是可能结果，不是测验已证明的技能；时机、措辞和别人是否愿意回应都会影响结果。

paragraphs.en: Repeated venting without a specific request may leave others unsure what to do. Repeated helping without a limit may leave you overcommitted. Consider whether you want acknowledgment, a change in the arrangement, a smaller role or simply room to stop.
paragraphs.zh: 反复吐槽却没有具体请求，可能让别人不知道怎样回应；反复帮忙却不设限，可能使自己承担过多。可以分清需要的是被听见、改变安排、缩小职责，还是停止的余地。

paragraphs.en: If appropriate, use two sentences for an ordinary issue: “The repeated changes are wearing me down. I can update this page once, but we need someone to confirm the final details.” Name what you can offer and what requires another agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 合适时，可以用两句话处理普通问题：“反复改动让我很累。这页我可以再更新一次，但最终细节需要有人确认。”分别说清能提供什么，以及什么还需要另行商定。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【THAN-K】人格。感恩者不是每天双手合十活得像心灵博主，而是您真的很容易先看到好的一面。别人对您一点小好，您会记很久；一次被接住、一句暖话、一点体面，都会在您心里留下痕迹。您看世界的滤镜并不一定粉红，但它至少没那么黑。您更愿意理解别人为什么这样做，也更容易把注意力放在那些“还不错”的细节上。这种人格在关系里通常让人舒服。因为您不会动不动就把人往坏处想，也不会轻易把一次失误定义成整段关系的死刑。您愿意给解释的机会，愿意给余地，也愿意承认别人曾经真心对您好过。当然，副作用也存在：您有时候会理解别人理解得太快，宽容别人宽容得太顺，以至于自己的委屈要延迟半拍才反应过来。但不管怎样，THAN-K 人格像一种温和的空气净化器，能在很多乌烟瘴气的关系里，保留一点人类相处的善意浓度。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew THAN-K. This character is not necessarily a motivational blogger living with hands permanently folded in gratitude. The story imagines someone who notices the good side first. A small kindness is remembered for a long time. Being caught when needed, hearing a warm sentence or being treated with a little dignity leaves a mark. The character's view of the world need not be rose-coloured, but neither is it entirely dark. They try to understand why another person acted that way and notice details that were at least reasonably good. This can make the character comfortable to spend time with. They do not immediately assume the worst or treat one mistake as a death sentence for the entire relationship. They allow an explanation, leave some room and acknowledge that another person has genuinely treated them kindly before. The portrait also includes a cost. Understanding can arrive so quickly, and forgiveness so smoothly, that the character recognises their own hurt half a beat late. Whatever the situation, the original ending likens THAN-K to a gentle air purifier, preserving a little goodwill in relationships that have become difficult to breathe in. Read this as a fictional combination of appreciation and possible over-accommodation. It does not establish moral goodness, require forgiveness or mean that gratitude should take priority over a clear boundary.

paragraphs.en: Sense of self: You broadly know your own way of doing things, even if your feelings sometimes wobble.

paragraphs.zh: 核心价值：你心里通常有一套自己的排序，做事不会完全靠别人推着走。
paragraphs.en: Core values: You usually have priorities of your own and do not rely entirely on other people to move you along.

paragraphs.zh: 依恋安全感：你在关系里更容易往善意方向理解别人，安全感偏温和型。
paragraphs.en: Relationship security: You tend to interpret others with goodwill and have a gentler approach to feeling secure in relationships.

paragraphs.zh: 情感投入度：你愿意投入感情，也会把感谢和回应表达出来。
paragraphs.en: Emotional investment: You are willing to invest emotionally and to express thanks and a response.

paragraphs.zh: 边界与依赖：你对边界和依赖的拿捏，不会一路失控，也不会完全无感。
paragraphs.en: Boundaries and dependence: Your approach to boundaries and dependence is neither continually out of control nor entirely detached.

paragraphs.zh: 世界观倾向：你看世界时会给人性和善意保留一点信用额度。
paragraphs.en: View of the world: Your view of the world leaves a little credit available for human kindness and goodwill.

paragraphs.zh: 规则与灵活度：你对规则不是死守，也不是彻底摆烂，更多是按场景调节。
paragraphs.en: Rules and flexibility: You neither follow rules rigidly nor abandon them entirely; you tend to adjust to the situation.

paragraphs.en: Life and meaning: You think about why people live as they do without necessarily thinking yourself into a dead end every day.

paragraphs.en: Social initiative: You need not be the loudest person in a group; you join in in a way that feels comfortable to you.

paragraphs.en: Interpersonal boundaries: You generally have a sense of interpersonal boundaries and know when to approach or step back.

paragraphs.zh: 表达与真实度：你表达自己时有筛选，不会把所有想法一次性全摊出来。
paragraphs.en: Authentic expression: You select what to express rather than laying out every thought at once.

title.en: An everyday scene for this portrait

paragraphs.en: During a busy afternoon, someone brings a document you had left behind. Later you say, “That saved me a return trip; thank you.” The acknowledgment names an observable action and its effect on you without making a sweeping claim about the person.
paragraphs.zh: 忙碌下午，有人送来你落下的文件。之后你说：“这让我少跑了一趟，谢谢。”感谢指出可见行动及对自己的帮助，不必顺势给对方作全面评价。

paragraphs.en: The same person may also miss an agreed deadline. You can appreciate the document and discuss the deadline separately. One helpful act does not create a debt, require trust in unrelated situations or cancel a request for something to change.
paragraphs.zh: 同一个人也可能错过商定期限。可以感谢送文件，同时另谈期限。一项帮助不产生债务，不要求在无关事情上信任，也不取消提出改变的资格。

paragraphs.en: Searching for something good in every situation can become pressure if it stops you naming disappointment. You do not owe a grateful interpretation of mistreatment. Appreciation is optional and can coexist with a boundary, an unresolved concern or a decision to leave.
paragraphs.zh: 如果因此无法说失望，凡事找好处也会变成压力。面对不当对待，不欠任何人感恩式解释。感谢是可选的，可以与边界、未解决的关切或离开的决定并存。

paragraphs.en: If you want to, identify one small action that helped and describe it plainly. You can thank the person, write a private note or do nothing further. Public praise, disclosure and contact are not necessary, particularly when a relationship feels uncomfortable.
paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，可以找一项确实有帮助的小行动，朴素描述。可以向对方感谢、写私人笔记，也可以不再行动。无需公开表扬、披露或联系，尤其在关系让人不舒服时。

paragraphs.en: Separately ask whether anything still needs discussion. Keeping these two observations apart can make the reflection clearer. You do not need to resolve a disagreement, forgive someone or feel a particular emotion to complete the guide.
paragraphs.zh: 另外再问，是否还有事需要讨论。把两种观察分开，能让反思更清楚。不必解决分歧、原谅谁或产生规定情绪，才能完成阅读。

paragraphs.en: Always rushing around, but somehow making it through.

paragraphs.zh: 动作快、反应快、生活感强，偶尔也显得乱。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait describes quick actions and reactions, strong everyday survival energy and occasional disorder.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【MALO】人格。吗喽不是贬义，它更像一种城市生存灵长类的最高形态：反应快、转身快、求生欲强、哪里有缝往哪里钻。您不一定最体面、最稳重、最像成年人模板，但您通常很能活，也很会在复杂现实里给自己找出路。别人遇事先慌，您会先动；别人想着面子，您想着怎么先把命续上。您的人生节奏看起来有点蹿、有点碎、有点随机，但偏偏总能越过大部分障碍。您像那种同时开了很多标签页的操作系统：看着乱，实际每一个都在跑。别人以为您瞎忙，您自己知道这是一种高密度应对生活的方式。您不靠高贵感活着，也不靠完美感撑场，而是靠灵活、靠机敏、靠一股子“今天不管怎样先混过去再说”的生命韧劲。吗喽人格的可爱之处就在于，它不一定优雅，但非常顽强；不一定高级，但特别能续航。别人追求高配人生，您擅长低电量模式下继续开机。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew MALO. The Chinese monkey-like nickname is used in the original as a comic urban survivor rather than a judgement of a person's value. This character reacts quickly, turns quickly and looks for any available opening. They need not be the most polished, settled or convincing example of an adult template, but tend to keep going and find a route through complicated circumstances. When someone else panics, the character moves. When someone else thinks about appearances, the character thinks about getting through the immediate situation. Life can look jumpy, fragmented and unpredictable, yet many obstacles are somehow crossed. The original image is an operating system with many tabs open: it looks disorganised, but each tab is doing something. Someone watching may see pointless busyness. The character experiences it as a concentrated way of responding to everyday demands. They do not rely on an air of nobility or an appearance of perfection. Flexibility, quick reactions and a determination to get through today keep the story moving. The original appeal is persistence without elegance: perhaps not glamorous, but able to continue running. While others pursue an upgraded life, this character keeps the system on in low-power mode. Treat the survival language as an entertainment metaphor. A result cannot establish resilience, living conditions, intelligence or whether a person should keep enduring an unreasonable load.

paragraphs.en: A small voluntary gathering loses its planned room. You look at the remaining time, people and available spaces, then suggest a shorter outdoor meeting if everyone wants it. You are adapting the plan rather than proving that the original plan never mattered.
paragraphs.zh: 小型自愿聚会的原定房间不能用了。你看剩余时间、参与者与可用地点，提议大家愿意时改为短一些的户外见面。这是在调整计划，不是证明原计划毫无意义。

paragraphs.en: Accessibility, weather or a participant’s preference may make that alternative unsuitable. Cancelling or postponing can be the workable decision. A temporary workaround does not override another person’s needs or the requirements that made the original venue important.
paragraphs.zh: 出入条件、天气或参与者偏好，可能让替代不合适。取消或延期也可以是可行决定。临时方案不取消他人的需要，也不替代原场地之所以重要的条件。

paragraphs.en: Rearranging what is available may preserve part of an activity when the first route closes. Whether it does is an outcome to inspect, not something the label guarantees. A modest alternative can be enough without pretending to reproduce everything originally planned.
paragraphs.zh: 重排现有条件，可能在原路不通时保住一部分活动；是否如此需要看结果，标签不保证。小一点的替代可以足够，无需假装完整复现最初计划。

paragraphs.en: A quick workaround can become confusing if nobody knows it is temporary. Name what it leaves out and when it should be reviewed. You can also stop adapting when each new patch creates more effort than the activity is worth to you.
paragraphs.zh: 临时办法若没说清暂时性，可能造成混乱。应说明缺什么、何时再看；如果每次补丁都让成本超过自己觉得值得的程度，也可以停止调整。

paragraphs.en: For one low-stakes disruption, identify what still matters and what can change. Suggest the smallest alternative that preserves that purpose, while naming any lost feature. Ask affected people rather than assuming they welcome the adaptation.
paragraphs.zh: 面对一次低风险中断，分清什么仍重要、什么能变。提出保住目的的最小替代，同时说清会失去什么，并问受影响的人，不假设大家欢迎调整。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, decide whether to keep, revise or discard it. There is no bonus for preserving a plan at all costs. This optional exercise does not replace professional procedures, safety checks or another person’s agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 之后决定保留、修改或放弃。无论代价都要保住计划，不会得到额外奖励。可选练习不替代专业规程、安全核对或他人同意。

paragraphs.zh: 你以为我是提款机，其实我是人形兜底系统。
paragraphs.en: You think I am a cash machine. I am really a human back-up system.

paragraphs.zh: 付出型倾向明显，资源和情感都偏愿意给人。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait emphasises giving resources and emotional support.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【ATM-er】人格。送钱者未必真的天天送钱，但一定常年在“支付”。支付时间、支付精力、支付耐心、支付情绪价值、支付那句“没事，我来”。别人还在斟酌要不要帮，您已经把钱、力气、注意力和责任感一起掏出来了。您在关系里的出厂设置就像自动扣款：只要把某个人或某件事划进“自己人”范围，付出就会变得异常顺手。这类人格给人的感觉通常很可靠，像一台老旧但坚固的 ATM 机，别人把焦虑、麻烦和缺口塞进去，您再“吐”出一点解决方案、一点兜底和一点安心。但问题也很明显：您太容易在关系里多掏一点，于是慢慢活成了人形结算中心。表面看您很大方、很够意思，实际上也会在深夜对着心里的账单叹一口气：为什么每次都是我？ATM-er 的伟大之处，在于真的能把很多关系撑住；危险之处，在于您有时会忘了，自己也不是无限额度。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew ATM-er, retained under the original code ATM. The giver need not literally hand out money every day, but in this portrait is almost always paying with something: time, effort, patience, emotional attention or another ‘It is all right; I will take care of it.’ While others consider whether to help, this character has already offered money, energy, attention and responsibility together. In the original story, relationships resemble an automatic payment setting. Once someone or something belongs to the character's inner circle, giving becomes exceptionally easy. That can feel reliable, like an old but sturdy cash machine: someone inserts anxiety, trouble or a missing piece, and the character supplies a little solution, support or reassurance. The difficulty is giving a little extra so often that the character gradually becomes a human settlement centre. Generosity looks effortless from outside, yet late at night an internal bill may prompt the question, ‘Why is it always me?’ The original portrait gives both admiration and caution. Giving can support many relationships; forgetting that one's own resources have limits is its danger. This entertainment result does not establish wealth, spending habits or an obligation to support anyone. Offering help and wanting support in return can coexist, and a fictional Giver label is not another person's claim on your resources.

paragraphs.en: A friend is moving and asks whether you can help. You offer one hour to label boxes because that fits your availability. The contribution is specific and freely chosen; it does not silently include transport, payment or staying until everything is finished.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友搬家问能否帮忙，你按自己的时间，提出用一小时标记箱子。投入具体且出于自愿，不默默包含交通、付款或必须留到全部结束。

paragraphs.en: The friend may prefer another kind of help or may decline. That response does not make your offer worthless. Asking what would actually help, and accepting the answer, is different from deciding for another person what they should need.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友可能更需要别的帮助，也可能婉拒，这不使提议失去价值。先问什么真正有用并接受回答，不同于替别人决定应该需要什么。

paragraphs.en: An appropriate contribution can support a shared activity, but its usefulness is an outcome to discuss. The theme cannot prove effectiveness or affection. An unsolicited offer is still an offer, and the recipient may not want it or owe a particular emotional response.
paragraphs.zh: 合适投入可能支持共同活动，但是否有用需要讨论实际结果。主题不能证明效果或感情。主动帮助仍是提议，对方可以不想要，也不欠规定的情绪回应。

paragraphs.en: Offering extra before checking capacity can make it difficult to change your mind later. If you notice resentment, exhaustion or a hidden expectation of return, examine the actual agreement. Giving does not require ignoring those signals or continuing an unwanted arrangement.
paragraphs.zh: 没核对余地就多承担，之后可能不好改口。发现怨气、疲惫或未说出的回报期待时，可以检查实际约定。付出不要求忽略这些信号，也不要求继续不想要的安排。

paragraphs.en: If useful, ask what would help before volunteering. State one contribution you freely want and can afford to make: “I can review this section tonight, but I cannot take the whole project.” Leave space for the other person to decline or suggest something else.
paragraphs.zh: 如果合适，可以先问需要什么，再主动承担。说出一项自愿且负担得起的投入：“今晚能帮看这一节，但不能接整个项目。”给对方拒绝或另提建议的空间。

paragraphs.en: After the task, consider whether the agreement remained clear and whether you want to repeat it. No exercise is necessary. You do not have to contact anyone, spend money or prove that your result deserves the word “giver.”
paragraphs.zh: 完成后，看约定是否一直清楚，以及是否还愿意再做。练习可不做，无需联系谁、花钱或证明自己配得上“付出者”名称。

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【THIN-K】人格。思考者的人生常常不是现场直播，而是延迟播出。别人看到一个现象就做反应，您看到一个现象先会问：为什么？还有没有别的解释？这事背后的逻辑是不是另一个逻辑的影子？您处理世界的方式不是“看见，行动”，而是“看见，思考，拆分，复盘，再思考，谨慎行动”。别人说您慢，您会觉得：急什么，我只是把脑子该走的流程走完。这种人格很强，因为它意味着您理解世界的深度往往比一般人更高。很多人只停留在表面感受，您却会本能地往深处再挖一层。副作用也很明显：您很容易把简单问题想复杂，把复杂问题想成论文，把关系里的小波动想出一个完整的精神宇宙。您脑子里的标签页经常多到能把自己电脑风扇烧起来。可也正因为如此，您一旦想明白，通常会比别人看得更远、更细、更不容易被表面带偏。别人靠直觉冲，您靠内部计算出手。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew THIN-K. The thinker's life in this portrait is not a live broadcast but a delayed transmission. Someone else notices a phenomenon and reacts. This character asks why it happened, whether another explanation exists, and whether the apparent logic is the shadow of some further logic. The sequence is not simply see and act. It is see, think, separate the parts, review, think again, then act cautiously. If called slow, the imagined answer is, ‘Why hurry? I am just letting my mind finish its process.’ The original story praises a desire to look below an immediate impression. Many people stop at a surface feeling; this character instinctively digs another layer down. The cost is clear too. A simple problem can become complicated, a complicated problem can become a dissertation, and a small fluctuation in a relationship can expand into a whole private universe. So many mental tabs remain open that the computer fan seems ready to burn out. Yet the story also imagines that, once a conclusion is reached, this long process can produce a more detailed view that is less easily led by appearances. Where another character rushes with intuition, THIN-K acts after internal calculation. This is the original flattering and teasing narrative, not evidence of intelligence, greater depth than other people or objectively better judgement.

paragraphs.en: Someone answers a long message with one sentence. Before deciding they are dismissing you, you consider time pressure, a different communication style or an unanswered part they missed. Those are possibilities to check, not facts the theme authorizes you to assume.

paragraphs.en: If the answer matters, a clear follow-up may provide more information than another private theory. Reflection can lead to asking, acting or leaving uncertainty alone. It does not require finding a charitable explanation for repeated poor treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 如果答案重要，一句明确追问可能比继续私下推想更有信息。思考可以通向询问、行动或保留未知；不要求为反复不当对待寻找善意解释。

paragraphs.en: Clarifying the question may prevent work on the wrong problem. Whether it does depends on what you actually discover. A detailed explanation can still be mistaken, and a quick answer can sometimes be adequate; the result does not reward complexity for its own sake.
paragraphs.zh: 厘清问题可能避免忙错方向，但是否如此取决于实际发现。详细解释也可能错，快速答案有时已足够；结果不为了复杂而奖励复杂。

paragraphs.en: Reopening every interpretation can make it hard to choose a next step. Ask whether another fact would change the decision or simply add detail. A temporary conclusion can include what remains unknown and when you would reconsider it.
paragraphs.zh: 不断重开每种理解，也可能使下一步难以确定。可以问再多一个事实会改变决定，还是只增加细节。暂时结论可以同时写明未知，以及何时重看。

paragraphs.en: For a small question, write three short lines: what you observed, one possible interpretation and one way to learn more. Mark the interpretation as provisional. You may choose no action if the issue does not matter enough to pursue.
paragraphs.zh: 面对小问题，写三行：看见什么、一种可能解释，以及一个获取信息的办法。把解释标作暂定。问题不值得继续时，也可以不采取行动。

paragraphs.zh: 按事情重要程度设停止点，再看是否厘清了什么。无需一直分析。本指南不诊断想太多，也不治疗持续困扰。

paragraphs.en: Much of the time, I can still rely on myself.

paragraphs.zh: 独处需求高，关系上的自给自足倾向更强。
paragraphs.en: The original portrait emphasises time alone and self-sufficiency in relationships.

paragraphs.zh: 恭喜您，您测出了【SOLO】人格。孤儿人格并不等于字面意义上的孤苦伶仃，而是一种很早就习惯“凡事自己来”的生存模式。遇到问题，您第一反应往往不是求助，而是先自己扛；情绪上来，您通常不是马上找人说，而是先关门、消化、整理、撑过去。您不是完全不需要别人，只是您太熟悉“最后还是得靠自己”这件事，所以很多依赖在您身上都自动被降级了。别人看您，会觉得您独、冷、边界重、不太好靠近，甚至有一点“你根本不需要谁”的气质。可事实上，SOLO 人格并不是什么都不想要，而是想要也不会轻易说。您很擅长在独处里完成自我修复，也很擅长在没人能接的时候把自己慢慢拎起来。您像一个长期单机运行的系统，不一定最热闹，但稳定性很高。别人靠群居回血，您靠沉默续命。别人说您不好亲近，您心里可能只会淡淡回一句：不是不想靠近，是我已经习惯先自己走一段。
paragraphs.en: Congratulations: you drew SOLO. The source's harsher orphan metaphor is not a literal claim about family circumstances. It describes a character who became used to handling things alone early on. A problem appears, and the first reaction is to carry it rather than ask for help. Feelings arrive, and the character closes the door to digest, organise and get through them before talking. This is not a complete absence of need for other people. The story imagines someone so familiar with ‘In the end, I still have to rely on myself’ that many forms of dependence have automatically been reduced. From outside, the character can look solitary, cold, strongly bounded or difficult to approach, almost as though they need nobody. Yet the portrait insists that not asking is different from wanting nothing. The character may want connection without easily saying so. They are accustomed to recovering alone and gradually lifting themselves when nobody else is there to catch them. The original image is a system that has run in single-player mode for a long time: not necessarily lively, but steady. Where someone else recharges in a group, SOLO keeps going in silence. If called hard to approach, the imagined answer is, ‘It is not that I never want closeness. I have simply become used to walking part of the way first.’ This is a fictional story, not evidence about family history, support needs or whether independence is always helpful.
